Gist of Int. F.M. 7699.

From Karen FINKELSTEIN, Berlin-Charlottenburg.
To Dr. Alexis FINKELSTEIN, 13, Shelford Park, Cambridge.
4.11.35.

Thanks them for their belated news. Hildemarie will no doubt soon have holidays again, in which to recover. Does father know that he should take oxygen baths . . . . . . . . . . . . Has had all sorts of business experiences. It is O.K. again with G., but she left the grain-merchant as he was away longer than he had said, and now he wishes to take legal steps against her. She had put herself out to help him till he found someone, then he explained that in the interval till she could legally leave, he would not let her go and would give her no money, so she simply got up and left. The South American journalist about whom she was so pleased, is charming one day and in a furious temper the next, but she is still working for him as long as he was away. To-day she had to go to the aerodrome for photographs - a very interesting but tiring job. Is now starting to work for a solicitor who represents important chemists. Although it is well paid, she will earn less there than with the South American. Perhaps she will find something else as well. She applied to a lawyer for a job, who refused her on sight. Thinks that he is quite mad. Hopes the South American will behave when he returns.

AW 8/11/35.
